A1.justification: Both complete 28-page PDFs describe PaAno and contain corresponding main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original PaAno benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity analyses and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains original PaAno benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity analyses and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The architecture, training objectives, memory bank and anomaly scoring remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies that the preceding patch lies w steps 'before' the anchor, replacing 'ahead'; both versions already specify a preceding patch, including in Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same TSB-AD-U and TSB-AD-M tasks and retain identical subset membership in Table 15. The Table 1 edit concerns sample-count reporting, assessed under E3.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain identical baseline rows in Tables 2–3 and 16–17. Appendix D also retains the same alternative encoders, losses and negative-selection strategies.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the reported TSB-AD-U Eval count from 530 to 350, matching the unchanged subset counts totaling 350 in Table 15. This corrects a stated evaluation sample size; the PDFs do not establish a changed split or rerun. Other evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4, Figure 5 and Appendix D retain the same component ablations and sensitivity analyses of architecture, losses, scheduling, memory-bank size, nearest neighbors, patch size and minibatch size. Appendix E's score-distribution analysis is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 repetitions with different random seeds in Section 4.1 and Appendix B.1, and retain identical mean and ± entries in Table 15. No uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: Detection scores, rankings, runtimes and qualitative findings remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Table 15 retains VUS-PR averages of 0.5296 for TSB-AD-U and 0.4263 for TSB-AD-M. The revised dataset count is covered under E3.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), formal assumptions and Appendix C's metric definitions remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 expands the loss subscripts from tri/pre to triplet/pretext without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about PaAno's patch-based representation learning, lightweight architecture, leading benchmark performance, efficiency and hyperparameter robustness.

C2.justification: The locality rationale, explanations of negative selection and early pretext training, online memory-bank update discussion and applicability claims remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Section 4.1, Appendix B and the reproducibility statement retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, tuning spaces, hardware and code-access information. The wording and loss-label corrections disclose no new implementation setting.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and research positioning are unchanged. Adding 'are' to the Chronos/MOMENT architecture sentence in Section 2.2 is a grammatical correction.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammatical and caption corrections, clarifies the preceding-patch wording in Section 3.3 and harmonizes Algorithm 1's loss names with the main text. The section and appendix organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: VUS-PR column headings gain bold emphasis in Table 4 and appendix tables, accompanied by small spacing and caption edits. Figures and table membership, numbering and placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the inconsistency between Table 1's evaluation count and Table 15's subset total, and removes ambiguous temporal wording in Section 3.3. Consistent loss names and modest table edits improve readability. These are useful reporting corrections, while the method, empirical evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
